card.name: A compact two‑story white‑brick home with
card.summary: A compact two‑story white‑brick home with a red shingle roof, front porch, sun room, and front garden, built to 1920s colonial proportions.
card.description: The two‑story residence occupies a compact 792 cm × 823 cm footprint, its white‑painted brick façade punctuated by dark‑tinted, slide‑open aluminum windows and a dignified red shingle roof that crowns a modest dormer. A welcoming front porch of pressure‑treated lumber stretches 300 cm wide, providing a shaded transition to the solid oak front door with traditional hinges. Inside, the ground floor hosts an open kitchen with oak cabinets, a dining alcove, a sun‑filled sun room, and a living area finished in warm plaster. Three well‑proportioned bedrooms and two full bathrooms are arranged on the second floor, accessed by a timber staircase with a sleek metal handrail. Shutters frame the dormer windows, adding a colonial charm, while a two‑car garage sits to the side, its steel roll‑up door sliding silently. The rear of the house is bordered by a low wooden fence that encloses a modest front garden, rich with soil, seasonal plantings, and a decorative edging. All structural elements—from the reinforced concrete slab to the timber roof trusses—are coordinated in a Revit BIM model, allowing precise LOD progression and fabrication data for each component. The home reads as a timeless yet functional blend of early‑20th‑century colonial aesthetics and modern livability.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions (792 cm × 823 cm) and confirm setbacks for the front garden and driveway.
Draft a site plan and floor plan in 2‑D, allocating 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, a sun room, a kitchen, living and dining areas, and a front porch.
Develop structural drawings for foundation, floor framing, wall studs, roof trusses, and stair stringers, then obtain building permits.
Order all long‑lead items (roof shingles, windows, doors, garage door) and schedule trades for foundation, framing, roofing, and rough‑in services.
Install exterior cladding, roof, windows, doors, and complete interior finishes such as drywall, flooring, and cabinetry.
Connect all mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, then landscape the front garden with soil, plants, and a low fence.
Perform a final inspection, apply paint touch‑ups, and hand over the completed two‑story red‑roofed home.
assumptions: Because the brief did not specify wall material or colour, the house is assumed to have white‑painted brick walls, a common choice for colonial‑style homes of the era.
The brief omitted the number of bedrooms and bathrooms; a typical six‑room two‑story plan from the reference designs was interpreted as three bedrooms and two full baths.
A two‑car attached garage is added as a standard amenity for modern residential expectations, even though the brief did not mention it.
The front garden is assumed to be a rectangular planting area of 5 m × 3 m with soil, ornamental shrubs, and a low wooden fence, providing the requested outdoor space.
questions: Should the front garden include any specific hardscape features such as a pathway, patio, or water element?
Do you prefer a particular style of interior finish (e.g., hardwood flooring versus carpet) for the main living areas?
Is there a requirement for any sustainable systems (solar panels, rainwater harvesting) that should be incorporated into the BIM model?
